precepts.text: Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth. A pastor claiming Christ was wrong for most of his life is the blind watchman in action.
precepts.point: Sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber; greedy dogs which can never have enough. One locked the church doors until he got his forty thousand, another promised millionaires overnight for a ten-thousand-dollar seed. All prosperity, no prophecy.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
“His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark.” We are supposed to watch and pray, to be alert to the times, to keep our spirit in order with the Most High and to repent. But the watchmen are blind. All these Christian apologists and Black pastors are ignorant. We are on the brink of civil war in America, and how many pastors are saying prepare ye war? None of them. They are celebrating Valentine's Day. They cannot bark: they will not prophesy and they will not warn you, like the dog that jumped out the window when its own owner pretended to break into the house.

They are “sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber”, silent and lazy, and “greedy dogs which can never have enough.” One pastor said nobody leaves until he gets his 40 G's, lock the doors. Another said sow a seed of ten thousand and you'll be a millionaire overnight. All they speak about is prosperity: nothing about prophecy, nothing about warning you, nothing about getting your spirit right. Many don't even think they have a reason to bark, because they are too comfortable to see the danger right in front of them.

Here is one of the watchmen in action. Jamal Bryant, senior pastor of New Birth Missionary Baptist Church, preached with conviction that 85% of Jesus's life he was wrong and out of order, doing what he was not called to do, and the people sat there and listened to it.

The Bible says sin is the transgression of the law, the breaking and violating of God's laws. So was Christ wrong? Peter answers: “Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.” He did no wrong at all.

Yet a pastor will get up and speak against Christ, and you never hear him speak against Babylon, America, never against homosexuality, never against the idolatrous festivals out here. That is the blind watchman, the dumb dog that cannot bark. So the prophets have to go out and proclaim among the Gentiles, “Prepare war”, and our own people need to know war is coming too.

precepts.text: Let not the son of the stranger that hath joined himself to the Lord say, The Lord hath utterly separated me from his people. The Lord which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him beside those that are gathered: the other sheep.
precepts.point: That is why there should be no Christian church: Christ died only for Israel. Everything they quote about Gentiles and the world has already been shown to be Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Isaiah 56 ties directly into Ephesians 2. The context is “my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed”: that is Christ.

“Neither let the son of the stranger, that hath joined himself to the Lord, speak, saying, The Lord hath utterly separated me from his people”. Who is that? The northern kingdom, the one the Lord cut off and called not his people. “neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree”: they could not bring forth children.

“Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the Lord, to serve him, and to love the name of the Lord, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant; Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer”. They say this means heathen will go into his house, and they will point to “an house of prayer for all people”. But read the next verse: “The Lord God which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him.”

The others are the other sheep: Christ said, I have other sheep not of this fold. Those gathered are this fold, and the others are the “all people” of the verse before. The son of the stranger in Isaiah 56 is the same as the strangers from the covenants of promise in Ephesians 2, who said the Lord had cut them off from his people. Now, in Christ, they are made nigh, grafted back in with their brothers, the natural branches.

precepts.text: They are greedy dogs that can never have enough and shepherds that cannot understand, every one looking to his own way and his own gain.
precepts.point: From the least to the greatest every one is given to covetousness, and from the prophet to the priest every one deals falsely, for the priests were only about gain at this time.

note.label: Jeremiah 6: The Ancient Nation from the North

precepts.why:
“Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter.” That is the prophet and the priest of Jeremiah's day: “from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely.” The priests were only about gain at this time, greedy dogs that can never have enough, every one looking to his own way and his own gain.

And it ran through the whole people: “from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness”. Shepherds that cannot understand cannot lead a people out of covetousness when they are given to it themselves.

precepts.text: His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark. A watchman is set to keep you out of harm's way, and one that cannot bark warns no one.
precepts.point: That is the condition of Israel as a nation right now. There is no shepherd, because the men our people look to for leadership are not shepherds according to the word.

note.label: Zechariah 10: Mine Anger Was Kindled Against the Shepherds

precepts.why:
They were troubled, because there was no shepherd. That is the condition of Israel as a nation right now, because the men our people look to for leadership are not shepherds according to the word. “His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark; sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber.”

A watchman is set to keep you out of harm's way, and one that cannot bark warns no one. Blind, ignorant, sleeping and loving to slumber: that is the leadership that leaves the flock going its own way, comforted in vain by idols and diviners.

precepts.text: Mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
precepts.point: He casts out them that sold and bought in the temple and overthrows the tables of the moneychangers, saying, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

note.label: Matthew 21: The King Cometh Meek, and the Kingdom Taken Away

precepts.why:
When Christ cast out them that sold and bought in the temple and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, he said, “It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.” Isaiah is where it is written: “for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.”

Isaiah speaks of the Most High bringing them to his holy mountain and making them “joyful in my house of prayer”, where their burnt offerings and sacrifices “shall be accepted upon mine altar”. The temple was given for prayer and for offerings that the Most High would accept, not for buying and selling.

So Christ was not acting on his own feelings. He held them to what was already written about his Father's house, and then the blind and the lame came to him in that same temple and he healed them.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why:
“His watchmen are blind”: his watchmen are our people, the Black and Latino leaders out here, blind because they cannot see with spiritual eyes. It is the same spirit as the Pharisees in John 11, who said if we let this man alone the Romans will come and take away our place and nation, our positions and our money.

“They are all ignorant”: spiritually ignorant of what the Bible says. “They are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark”: a watchdog is the first line of warning, danger’s coming, master, wake up. These cannot warn anybody about the impending doom the Bible prophesies. “Sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber”: loving to slumber in their sin.
